newsitem.title: USA: Montana seeding, reseeding slowed by precipitation.
newsitem.headline: Montana seeding, reseeding slowed by precipitation.

text.p: Precipitation slowed seeding or reseeding of small grains in a few areas of Montana, with scattered hail damage noted late in the week, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly update.
There were 5.5 days suitable for fieldwork during the week ended Sunday.
Spring wheat in boot 3 pct vs 0 w/a, 3 y/a, 6 average.
Spring wheat rated 56 percent good to excellent versus 64 last week, 37 pct fair vs 32 last week.
Barley in boot 13 pct vs 13 w/a, 2 y/a, 6 avg.
Barley rated 62 percent good to excellent versus 72 last week, 33 pct fair vs 26 last week.
Winter wheat rated 57 percent good to excellent versus 57 last week, 32 pct fair vs 29 last week, and 11 pct poor or very poor vs 14 last week.
Corn emerged 97 pct vs 86 w/a, 83 y/a, avg unavailable.
Oats emerged 88 pct vs 77 w/a, 80 y/a, 86 avg.
Oats rated 53 percent good to excellent versus 53 last week, 38 pct fair vs 44 last week.
Sugarbeets emerged 100 pct vs 100 w/a, 100 y/a, avg unavail.

Pasture and range were rated 56 percent good to excellent, versus 54 percent a week earlier. Topsoil moisture was rated 11 percent very short, 22 pct short, 65 pct adequate, 2 pct surplus. Subsoils were rated 5 pct very short, 20 pct short, 73 pct adequate, 2 pct surplus.
